chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'Our companions hunt the gazelle, so I eat its meat.' He said: 'If it has a tusk, do not eat it.' He then paused for a moment, and when I was about to rise, he said: 'As for you, I dislike for you to eat it, so do not eat it.'

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike (indicating a recommended avoidance or karahat)
key_terms.نَابٌ: Tusk (specifically referring to the upper canine tooth of the male gazelle)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating gazelle meat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the distinction between obligatory prohibition (haram) and recommended dislike (karahat) in Shia jurisprudence, where the presence of a tusk renders the meat impermissible while the general consumption is merely disliked for the specific narrator. It highlights the nuanced legal reasoning of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in differentiating between intrinsic defects in the animal and contextual preferences for the consumer. This ruling is foundational for understanding the criteria of 'cleanliness' (tayyibat) in hunted game within the Ja'fari school of thought.
